newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan premier takes nuclear appeal to public.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan premier takes nuclear appeal to public.

text.p: Taiwan's premier, barred by the opposition from defending a controversial nuclear power project in parliament, appealed directly for public support on Thursday on the eve of a do-or-die vote.

"This is a choice we cannot afford not to make," Premier Lien Chan said in an unscheduled appeal broadcast on live television and radio. He was referring to construction of Taiwan's politically stalemated fourth nuclear power station.

Lien, a lightning rod for attacks by the main opposition Democratic Progressive Party and who doubles as vice president, spoke at a podium hastily erected on the steps of the Taipei headquarters of the Executive Yuan, Taiwan's cabinet.

Suggesting a possible compromise in a high-stakes dispute that has dragged on for months, Lien stressed the need for the fourth plant already under construction but hinted that his government would not seek to build a fifth.
"Judging from Taiwan's natural environment and society's responses, the chances are very small for us to build a fifth nuclear power plant," Lien said.

Lien called Friday's parliamentary vote on whether to cancel the project "very important" for Taiwan with ramifications for the island's global image, but made no direct reference to Tuesday's opposition move to bar him from entering parliament to defend the project.
